clusters.description: Rain from a faint drizzle to a violent downpour; expressions differ in how hard the rain falls, how it sounds, and whether they are everyday or literary.

expressions.nuance: A fine, misty drizzle you feel on your skin more than see falling.

example.ja: 外に出ると、細かい霧雨で眼鏡がすぐに曇った。
example.en: When I stepped outside, the fine drizzle fogged my glasses at once.

expressions.nuance: Light rain; the plain word for a gentle but real shower, lighter than 本降り.

example.ja: 朝から小雨が降ったりやんだりしている。
example.en: A light rain has been coming and going since morning.

expressions.nuance: Mimetic for soft, steady, quiet rain, often with a calm or melancholy mood.

example.ja: 梅雨の雨が一日中しとしとと降り続いた。
example.en: The rainy-season rain fell softly all day long.

expressions.nuance: Scattered, sparse drops, typically as rain starts or stops, rather than steady rain.

example.ja: 空が暗くなって、雨がぱらぱらと降り出した。
example.en: The sky darkened and a few drops of rain began to fall.

expressions.nuance: To start raining; focuses on the moment the rain begins.

example.ja: 駅に着いたとたん、急に雨が降り出した。
example.en: The moment I reached the station, it suddenly started to rain.

expressions.nuance: The pace or force of the rain, used with 強まる/弱まる to describe it changing.

example.ja: 夜になって雨足がだんだん強まってきた。
example.en: As night fell, the rain gradually grew heavier.

expressions.nuance: Rain that has settled in properly and will not stop soon, as opposed to a passing sprinkle.

example.ja: 夕方から本降りになり、傘なしでは歩けなくなった。
example.en: From evening it rained in earnest and you couldn't walk without an umbrella.

expressions.nuance: A sudden, short shower that catches people unprepared.

example.ja: 帰り道でにわか雨に降られて服がぬれた。
example.en: I got caught in a sudden shower on the way home and my clothes got wet.

expressions.nuance: A heavy summer afternoon shower, often with thunder, that clears quickly.

example.ja: 夏の午後、激しい夕立のあとで涼しい風が吹いた。
example.en: After a fierce summer afternoon shower, a cool wind blew.

expressions.nuance: The long early-summer rains of the rainy season; poetic and seasonal.

example.ja: 五月雨が音もなく古い庭をぬらしている。
example.en: The early-summer rain silently wets the old garden.

expressions.nuance: Mimetic for loud, pouring rain; you hear it as much as see it.

example.ja: 外は雨がざあざあ降っていて、出かける気になれない。
example.en: It's pouring outside and I don't feel like going out.

expressions.nuance: Heavy rain in a matter-of-fact, news-report sense, usually with consequences.

example.ja: 昨夜の大雨で、朝の電車が一時止まった。
example.en: Last night's heavy rain briefly stopped the morning trains.

expressions.nuance: A drenching downpour; vivid and everyday, stronger in feel than 大雨.

example.ja: 土砂降りの中を、傘もささずに走って帰った。
example.en: I ran home through the downpour without an umbrella.

expressions.nuance: Rain so heavy it falls like thick bamboo stalks; a written, dramatic image.

example.ja: 篠突く雨の中、彼は黙って門の前に立っていた。
example.en: In the driving rain, he stood silently before the gate.

clusters.description: The hours of darkness from evening to the dead of night; expressions differ by how late it is, how dark or still it feels, and how literary the image is.

expressions.nuance: The night sky; a neutral scene-setting word.

example.ja: 澄んだ夜空に、大きな満月が浮かんでいる。
example.en: A big full moon floats in the clear night sky.

expressions.nuance: Moonlight as a source of light in the dark.

example.ja: 街灯のない山道を、月明かりを頼りに歩いた。
example.en: I walked the unlit mountain path by moonlight.

expressions.nuance: The middle of the night; the everyday word for the hours when people sleep.

example.ja: 物音がして、夜中に目が覚めてしまった。
example.en: A noise woke me up in the middle of the night.

expressions.nuance: Early evening just after dark; a slightly old-fashioned, poetic word.

example.ja: 宵の空に、一番星が小さく光っていた。
example.en: The first star was shining faintly in the evening sky.

expressions.nuance: Late at night, when the night has worn on; softer and more atmospheric than 深夜.

example.ja: 面白くて、夜更けまでその本を読んでいた。
example.en: It was so gripping that I read the book late into the night.

expressions.nuance: Of night: to grow late and deep; used as 夜が更ける.

example.ja: 昔話をしているうちに、すっかり夜が更けた。
example.en: While we talked about old times, the night grew late.

expressions.nuance: Late night around and after midnight; factual, used for times and schedules.

example.ja: 深夜のコンビニは、客がほとんどいない。
example.en: Late-night convenience stores have hardly any customers.

expressions.nuance: All night long, without stopping until morning.

example.ja: 締め切りに間に合わせるため、夜通し作業した。
example.en: I worked all night to make the deadline.

expressions.nuance: Of a house or town: to fall quiet because everyone is asleep.

example.ja: 家族が寝静まってから、そっと家を出た。
example.en: After my family had fallen asleep, I quietly left the house.

expressions.nuance: The dead of night; more emphatic and dramatic than 夜中.

example.ja: 真夜中に突然、電話のベルが鳴った。
example.en: In the dead of night, the phone suddenly rang.

expressions.nuance: Pitch dark, with no light at all.

example.ja: 停電で、部屋の中が一瞬で真っ暗になった。
example.en: In the blackout the room went pitch dark in an instant.

expressions.nuance: Darkness as a presence; heavier and more ominous than 暗さ.

example.ja: 車のライトが、山道の深い闇を照らした。
example.en: The car's headlights lit up the deep darkness of the mountain road.

expressions.nuance: The veil of night falling over the world; a written, poetic image.

example.ja: 夜の帳が下りると、港町に灯がともった。
example.en: As night's curtain fell, lights came on in the port town.

expressions.nuance: The small hours around 2–3 a.m., traditionally the eeriest time of night.

example.ja: 丑三つ時に、廊下から不気味な物音がした。
example.en: In the dead of night, an eerie sound came from the hallway.

clusters.description: What a face shows, from subtle shifts to dramatic changes; expressions differ by the feeling conveyed (displeasure, surprise, shyness, shock) and how visible it is.

expressions.nuance: Expressionless; showing no feeling at all, which can seem cold.

example.ja: 彼は最後まで無表情のまま話を聞いていた。
example.en: He listened to the end with a blank expression.

expressions.nuance: A straight, serious face, often contrasted with joking.

example.ja: 兄はいつも真顔でつまらない冗談を言う。
example.en: My brother always tells silly jokes with a straight face.

expressions.nuance: Complexion, and the feelings it betrays; 顔色を変える means to visibly react.

example.ja: 悪い知らせにも、彼女は顔色ひとつ変えなかった。
example.en: Even at the bad news, she didn't bat an eye.

expressions.nuance: To narrow the eyes, usually in fondness or quiet pleasure.

example.ja: 祖母は孫の寝顔を見て、目を細めた。
example.en: Grandmother smiled fondly at her grandchild's sleeping face.

expressions.nuance: To pout, showing childish discontent.

example.ja: おもちゃを取り上げられて、子どもは口をとがらせた。
example.en: When his toy was taken away, the child pouted.

expressions.nuance: To knit the brows in disapproval at something distasteful; about judgment rather than pain.

example.ja: 電車で騒ぐ若者に、老人は眉をひそめた。
example.en: The old man frowned at the young people making noise on the train.

expressions.nuance: To grimace from pain, a bad taste or annoyance; more physical than 眉をひそめる.

example.ja: 薬があまりに苦くて、思わず顔をしかめた。
example.en: The medicine was so bitter that I grimaced in spite of myself.

expressions.nuance: For one's face to cloud over with worry or sadness.

example.ja: 父の病気のことを聞いて、母は顔を曇らせた。
example.en: My mother's face clouded over when she heard about Dad's illness.

expressions.nuance: To go wide-eyed with surprise.

example.ja: 値段を聞いて、友人は目を丸くしていた。
example.en: My friend's eyes went wide when he heard the price.

expressions.nuance: To blush with shyness or embarrassment; a gentle, written image.

example.ja: 思いがけず褒められて、彼女は頬を染めた。
example.en: Praised unexpectedly, she blushed.

expressions.nuance: A sullen, sour face that makes displeasure obvious to everyone.

example.ja: 兄は朝から仏頂面で、誰とも話さない。
example.en: My brother has had a sour face since morning and won't talk to anyone.

expressions.nuance: To turn pale from fear or shock.

example.ja: 事故の知らせを聞いて、彼はさっと青ざめた。
example.en: He turned pale at once at news of the accident.

expressions.text: 苦虫を噛み潰したよう
expressions.reading: にがむしをかみつぶしたよう
expressions.nuance: Looking as if one had bitten a bitter bug: a deeply sour, disgusted face.

example.ja: 報告を聞いた部長は、苦虫を噛み潰したような顔をした。
example.en: Hearing the report, the manager looked thoroughly sour.

clusters.description: From a faint smile to helpless laughter; expressions differ in volume, whether the laugh is warm, sly, wry or mocking, and how physical it is.

expressions.nuance: To smile gently without a sound; warm and composed.

example.ja: 赤ちゃんが母親の顔を見て、にこっと微笑んだ。
example.en: The baby looked at its mother's face and smiled.

expressions.nuance: A single broad, pleasant smile, often in greeting.

example.ja: 店に入ると、店員がにっこり笑って迎えてくれた。
example.en: When I entered the shop, the clerk greeted me with a big smile.

expressions.nuance: Smiling continuously and cheerfully; describes a sunny disposition or mood.

example.ja: 祖父はいつもにこにこして、孫の話を聞いている。
example.en: Grandfather always listens to his grandchildren with a smile.

expressions.nuance: Suppressed giggling, trying to keep quiet.

example.ja: 授業中、後ろの席でくすくす笑う声がした。
example.en: During class, I heard giggling from the seats behind me.

expressions.nuance: A knowing smirk or grin, often slightly unpleasant or hinting at a secret.

example.ja: 弟は何かをたくらんでいるように、にやにやしている。
example.en: My brother is smirking as if he's up to something.

expressions.nuance: A wry, bitter smile at something awkward or embarrassing.

example.ja: 自分の失敗を指摘されて、苦笑いするしかなかった。
example.en: When my mistake was pointed out, all I could do was smile wryly.

expressions.nuance: Laughter that slips out despite oneself at something foolish; slightly derisive.

example.ja: 大臣の的外れな発言に、会場から失笑が漏れた。
example.en: The minister's off-the-mark remark drew stifled laughter from the hall.

expressions.nuance: To burst out laughing suddenly, unable to hold it in.

example.ja: あまりにおかしくて、会議中に思わず吹き出した。
example.en: It was so funny that I burst out laughing in the middle of the meeting.

expressions.nuance: Loud, unrestrained guffawing.

example.ja: お笑い番組を見ながら、家族でげらげら笑った。
example.en: The whole family guffawed watching a comedy show.

expressions.nuance: A big, hearty laugh; the plain strong word.

example.ja: 昔の写真を見て、みんなで大笑いした。
example.en: We all had a good laugh looking at old photos.

expressions.nuance: An explosion of laughter, typically from a whole group or audience.

example.ja: 彼の最初の一言で、会場が爆笑に包まれた。
example.en: His very first remark had the whole hall roaring with laughter.

expressions.nuance: A loud, haughty laugh, often triumphant or villainous.

example.ja: 悪役が舞台の真ん中で勝ち誇って高笑いした。
example.en: The villain laughed triumphantly in the middle of the stage.

expressions.nuance: To hold one's sides laughing; laughter so strong it hurts.

example.ja: 彼の失敗談に、みんな腹を抱えて笑った。
example.en: Everyone doubled over laughing at the story of his blunder.

expressions.nuance: To roll about laughing, helpless with laughter.

example.ja: 子どもたちは床の上で、いつまでも笑い転げていた。
example.en: The children kept rolling around on the floor laughing.

clusters.description: From eyes welling up to breaking down in sobs; expressions differ in volume, whether tears are held back, and how physical or literary the image is.

expressions.nuance: To have tears come to one's eyes without actually crying.

example.ja: 息子からの手紙を読んで、母は涙ぐんだ。
example.en: Reading the letter from her son, my mother teared up.

expressions.nuance: Of the eyes: to grow moist and glisten with emotion; gentle, often touching.

example.ja: お礼を言う彼女の目は、少し潤んでいた。
example.en: Her eyes were a little moist as she thanked us.

expressions.nuance: Of a child: to screw up the face and be on the verge of crying.

example.ja: 弟は公園で転んで、べそをかいていた。
example.en: My little brother fell in the park and was about to cry.

expressions.nuance: Whimpering and moping weakly; often used critically.

example.ja: いつまでもめそめそしていないで、前を向こう。
example.en: Stop moping and look forward.

expressions.nuance: To hold back tears through effort.

example.ja: 彼は唇をかんで、必死に涙をこらえていた。
example.en: He bit his lip, desperately holding back tears.

expressions.nuance: Quiet, continuous sobbing, often alone.

example.ja: 隣の部屋で、誰かがしくしく泣いている。
example.en: Someone is quietly sobbing in the next room.

expressions.nuance: To sob with sniffling, trying to muffle the sound.

example.ja: 葬儀の会場のあちこちで、すすり泣く声がした。
example.en: Muffled sobs could be heard throughout the funeral hall.

expressions.nuance: Of tears: falling in big drops one after another.

example.ja: 話しているうちに、大粒の涙がぽろぽろこぼれた。
example.en: As she spoke, big tears rolled down one after another.

expressions.nuance: To sob convulsively, catching one's breath; typical of children.

example.ja: 迷子になった子が、駅で泣きじゃくっている。
example.en: A lost child is sobbing uncontrollably at the station.

expressions.nuance: Bawling loudly and openly.

example.ja: おもちゃが壊れて、妹はわんわん泣き出した。
example.en: When her toy broke, my little sister burst out bawling.

expressions.nuance: Crying loudly and hard; common today for being deeply moved.

example.ja: 映画の最後の場面で、思わず号泣してしまった。
example.en: I sobbed my heart out at the last scene of the film.

expressions.nuance: To collapse in tears, overwhelmed by grief.

example.ja: 悲しい知らせを聞いて、彼女はその場に泣き崩れた。
example.en: At the sad news, she broke down in tears on the spot.

expressions.nuance: Choked sobbing; a written word for grief that cannot be held in.

example.ja: 静まり返った部屋に、彼女の嗚咽だけが響いた。
example.en: Only her sobbing echoed through the silent room.

expressions.nuance: To spend one's days in tears, lost in grief.

example.ja: 夫を亡くした彼女は、何日も涙に暮れた。
example.en: After losing her husband, she spent days in tears.

clusters.description: Ways of moving on foot; expressions differ by pace, mood (aimless, dejected, proud, stealthy) and steadiness.

expressions.nuance: A walk for pleasure or exercise.

example.ja: 夕食の後、犬を連れて川沿いを散歩した。
example.en: After dinner I walked the dog along the river.

expressions.nuance: To go somewhere in person, implying effort or repeated visits.

example.ja: 説明を聞くために、何度も現場に足を運んだ。
example.en: I went to the site many times to hear the explanation.

expressions.nuance: Strolling aimlessly with no set destination.

example.ja: 休みの日は、商店街をぶらぶら歩くのが好きだ。
example.en: On my days off I like to wander around the shopping street.

expressions.nuance: To wander about idly; the verb form of ぶらぶら.

example.ja: 待ち合わせまで、駅前を少しぶらついた。
example.en: I hung around by the station for a while before meeting up.

expressions.nuance: Plodding steadily on foot over a fair distance.

example.ja: バスがないので、駅まで二十分てくてく歩いた。
example.en: There was no bus, so I trudged twenty minutes to the station.

expressions.nuance: Walking briskly without looking around or stopping.

example.ja: 彼は挨拶もせずに、すたすたと行ってしまった。
example.en: He walked briskly off without even saying hello.

expressions.nuance: Trudging slowly and dejectedly.

example.ja: 試合に負けて、選手たちはとぼとぼ帰っていった。
example.en: After losing the match, the players trudged home.

expressions.nuance: Stealthy tiptoeing so as not to be heard.

example.ja: 寝ている赤ちゃんを起こさないよう、忍び足で歩いた。
example.en: I tiptoed so as not to wake the sleeping baby.

expressions.nuance: The weaving gait of a drunk.

example.ja: 飲み会の帰り、父は千鳥足で帰ってきた。
example.en: After the drinking party, my father came home staggering.

expressions.nuance: To stagger or totter, losing balance.

example.ja: 疲れ切った彼は、よろめきながら坂を上った。
example.en: Utterly exhausted, he staggered up the slope.

expressions.nuance: To walk or tread; mostly figurative for following a path in life.

example.ja: 彼は周りに流されず、自分の信じる道を歩んできた。
example.en: He has walked the path he believes in, without following the crowd.

expressions.nuance: To wander lost or without purpose.

example.ja: 道に迷って、暗い森の中を何時間もさまよった。
example.en: I got lost and wandered for hours in the dark forest.

expressions.nuance: To parade slowly through the streets, as in a festival procession.

example.ja: 祭りの日には、神輿が町じゅうを練り歩く。
example.en: On festival day, the portable shrine parades all through the town.

expressions.nuance: Striding proudly and freely, as if one owns the place.

example.ja: おしゃれな若者たちが、大通りを闊歩している。
example.en: Stylish young people are striding proudly along the main street.

clusters.description: Ways of looking at something; expressions differ by duration (glance vs stare), direction, attention, and the attitude behind the look.

expressions.nuance: A single brief glance; written, often implying indifference.

example.ja: 彼は私を一瞥しただけで、何も言わずに去った。
example.en: He merely glanced at me and left without a word.

expressions.nuance: A quick, casual, fleeting glance.

example.ja: 話の途中で、彼女は時計をちらっと見た。
example.en: In the middle of the conversation, she glanced at the clock.

expressions.nuance: To peek through a gap or into something.

example.ja: ドアの隙間から、そっと部屋の中を覗いた。
example.en: I quietly peeked into the room through the gap in the door.

expressions.nuance: To look up at something.

example.ja: 芝生に寝転んで、星のきれいな夜空を見上げた。
example.en: I lay on the grass and looked up at the starry night sky.

expressions.nuance: To gaze at a view at leisure, taking in the whole scene.

example.ja: ホテルの窓から、ぼんやりと海を眺めた。
example.en: I gazed absently at the sea from the hotel window.

expressions.nuance: To look out over a wide area.

example.ja: 山頂からは、ふもとの町を一望に見渡せる。
example.en: From the summit you can look out over the whole town below.

expressions.nuance: Fixedly, without moving the eyes.

example.ja: 猫が窓辺から、庭の鳥をじっと見ている。
example.en: From the windowsill, the cat is watching a bird in the garden intently.

expressions.nuance: To stare at steadily, often with emotion or concentration.

example.ja: 彼は何も言わずに、私の目をじっと見つめた。
example.en: Without a word, he looked steadily into my eyes.

expressions.nuance: To strain one's eyes to make out something hard to see.

example.ja: 暗闇の中で目を凝らすと、人影が見えた。
example.en: Straining my eyes in the dark, I made out a figure.

expressions.nuance: To be absorbed in watching something.

example.ja: 子どもたちは息をのんで手品に見入っていた。
example.en: The children were holding their breath, absorbed in the magic trick.

expressions.nuance: To be captivated, watching something beautiful in a daze.

example.ja: あまりに美しい夕日に、しばらく見とれていた。
example.en: I stood entranced for a while by the beautiful sunset.

expressions.nuance: To glare at someone in anger or suspicion.

example.ja: 彼は何も言わずに、相手を鋭く睨んだ。
example.en: Without a word, he glared sharply at the other man.

expressions.nuance: Intent, unwavering staring; written and clinical in tone.

example.ja: 彼は画面を凝視したまま、まったく動かない。
example.en: He stays completely still, staring at the screen.

expressions.nuance: To have one's eyes captured by something striking.

example.ja: 公園に入ったとたん、満開の桜に目を奪われた。
example.en: As soon as I entered the park, the cherry blossoms in full bloom captivated me.

clusters.description: Ways of saying things; expressions differ by volume, formality, the speaker's attitude (confiding, insisting, hesitating) and how forceful the speech is.

expressions.nuance: Humble 'to say', used toward superiors and in formal speech.

example.ja: 皆様のご協力に、心よりお礼申し上げます。
example.en: I offer my heartfelt thanks to all of you for your cooperation.

expressions.nuance: To state or express formally, as in a meeting or in writing.

example.ja: 会議では、それぞれが自分の意見を述べた。
example.en: At the meeting, each person stated their opinion.

expressions.nuance: To say or mention aloud, often something usually left unsaid.

example.ja: 彼は苦しい時でも、不満を一度も口にしなかった。
example.en: Even in hard times, he never once voiced a complaint.

expressions.nuance: To chat or talk casually, sometimes too much.

example.ja: 久しぶりに会った友達と、一晩中しゃべった。
example.en: I chatted all night with a friend I hadn't seen in ages.

expressions.nuance: To mutter to oneself.

example.ja: 窓の外を見て、「寒そうだな」と彼はつぶやいた。
example.en: Looking out the window, he muttered, 'Looks cold.'

expressions.nuance: To whisper, usually intimately or secretly.

example.ja: 彼女は私の耳元で、そっと秘密をささやいた。
example.en: She softly whispered a secret in my ear.

expressions.nuance: To tell or relate at length, like a story or experience.

example.ja: 祖父は若い頃の戦争の体験を静かに語った。
example.en: Grandfather quietly told of his wartime experiences as a young man.

expressions.nuance: To confide something one has kept to oneself.

example.ja: ずっと隠していた悩みを、親友に打ち明けた。
example.en: I confided to my best friend a worry I'd long kept hidden.

expressions.nuance: To broach a difficult subject.

example.ja: 言いにくい話を、なかなか切り出せなかった。
example.en: I just couldn't bring myself to raise the awkward subject.

expressions.nuance: To mumble or falter, hesitating to say something.

example.ja: 遅刻の理由を聞かれて、彼は口ごもった。
example.en: When asked why he was late, he faltered.

expressions.nuance: To insist stubbornly on a claim.

example.ja: 証拠があるのに、彼は自分は悪くないと言い張った。
example.en: Despite the evidence, he insisted he wasn't to blame.

expressions.nuance: To rattle on rapidly without letting others speak.

example.ja: 彼女は相手に口を挟ませず、早口でまくしたてた。
example.en: She rattled on at high speed, not letting the other person get a word in.

expressions.nuance: To declare flatly and bluntly, without caring about the effect.

example.ja: 彼は「二度とここには来ない」と言い放った。
example.en: He declared flatly, 'I'm never coming here again.'

expressions.nuance: To shout angrily at someone.

example.ja: 約束を破った息子を、父は大声で怒鳴った。
example.en: Father shouted loudly at his son for breaking his promise.

clusters.description: Ways of eating; expressions differ by politeness, how much and how fast one eats, and whether the focus is enjoyment or appetite.

expressions.nuance: Humble 'to eat', and the set phrase said before a meal.

example.ja: せっかくなので、遠慮なくいただきます。
example.en: Since you've gone to the trouble, I'll gladly help myself.

expressions.nuance: Honorific 'to eat', used for someone else's eating.

example.ja: どうぞ、温かいうちに召し上がってください。
example.en: Please eat it while it's warm.

expressions.nuance: To nibble or snack on something with the fingers.

example.ja: 仕事の合間に、机の上のお菓子をつまんだ。
example.en: Between tasks, I snacked on the sweets on my desk.

expressions.nuance: Chewing with the mouth closed; cute and small-scale.

example.ja: ハムスターがひまわりの種をもぐもぐ食べている。
example.en: The hamster is munching on sunflower seeds.

expressions.nuance: To have a small appetite.

example.ja: 祖母は年を取って、最近食が細くなった。
example.en: My grandmother has grown older and eats less these days.

expressions.nuance: To savor, paying attention to the taste.

example.ja: 旅先で、旬の魚の味をゆっくり味わった。
example.en: On my trip I slowly savored the seasonal fish.

expressions.nuance: To relish delicious food with evident pleasure.

example.ja: 旅館で、地元の新鮮な料理に舌鼓を打った。
example.en: At the inn, we feasted happily on fresh local dishes.

expressions.nuance: Of food: so good that one keeps eating.

example.ja: このおかずはご飯に合って、つい箸が進む。
example.en: This dish goes so well with rice that I can't stop eating.

expressions.nuance: To stuff one's cheeks full.

example.ja: 遠足で、子どもが大きなおにぎりを頬張っている。
example.en: On the school trip, a child is stuffing his cheeks with a big rice ball.

expressions.nuance: Eating heartily in big bites, with good appetite.

example.ja: お腹がすいていた弟は、ご飯をぱくぱく食べた。
example.en: My hungry little brother gobbled up his rice.

expressions.nuance: To polish off a whole plate.

example.ja: 彼は大盛りのカレーを、あっという間に平らげた。
example.en: He polished off a large curry in no time.

expressions.nuance: To shovel food into one's mouth in a hurry.

example.ja: 遅刻しそうだったので、ご飯をかき込んで家を出た。
example.en: I was about to be late, so I shoveled down my rice and left.

expressions.nuance: Wolfing food greedily, as if starving.

example.ja: 部活の後、腹をすかせた彼はがつがつ食べた。
example.en: After club practice, he wolfed down his food, starving.

expressions.nuance: To devour greedily; written, and also used figuratively (むさぼるように読む).

example.ja: 飢えた旅人は、差し出されたパンをむさぼった。
example.en: The starving traveler devoured the bread he was offered.

clusters.description: Wind from a gentle breeze to a howling gale; expressions differ in strength, sound, season and whether they are everyday or poetic.

expressions.nuance: A gentle, pleasant breeze.

example.ja: 開けた窓から、気持ちのいいそよ風が入ってきた。
example.en: A pleasant breeze came in through the open window.

expressions.nuance: Mimetic for wind blowing softly and pleasantly.

example.ja: 川辺では、春の風がそよそよと吹いている。
example.en: By the river, the spring wind is blowing softly.

expressions.nuance: Of plants: to rustle and sway in a light breeze.

example.ja: 秋の田んぼで、稲穂が風にそよいでいる。
example.en: In the autumn paddies, the ears of rice sway in the breeze.

expressions.nuance: Of wind or sea: to die down and become calm.

example.ja: 夕方になると風が凪いで、海が静かになった。
example.en: In the evening the wind died down and the sea grew calm.

expressions.nuance: Of wind: to blow right through a space.

example.ja: 窓を開けると、涼しい風が廊下を吹き抜けた。
example.en: When I opened the windows, a cool wind blew through the corridor.

expressions.nuance: To cut through the wind with speed.

example.ja: 自転車で風を切って、坂道を下っていった。
example.en: I sped down the hill on my bike, cutting through the wind.

expressions.nuance: The first strong southerly wind of spring.

example.ja: 今日、関東地方で春一番が吹いたそうだ。
example.en: Apparently the first spring gale blew in the Kanto region today.

expressions.nuance: The cold, dry wind of early winter that strips the trees.

example.ja: 木枯らしが吹いて、街路樹の葉がすっかり落ちた。
example.en: The wintry wind blew and the roadside trees lost all their leaves.

expressions.nuance: Mimetic for a thin, whistling wind.

example.ja: 一晩中、北風が窓の外でひゅうひゅう鳴っていた。
example.en: All night, the north wind whistled outside the window.

expressions.nuance: Mimetic for a strong, howling wind; heavier than ひゅうひゅう.

example.ja: 台風が近づき、外は風がびゅうびゅう吹いている。
example.en: The typhoon is approaching and the wind is howling outside.

expressions.nuance: A sudden gust.

example.ja: 急な突風で、さしていた傘が壊れてしまった。
example.en: A sudden gust of wind broke the umbrella I was holding.

expressions.nuance: Strong wind, as in weather reports.

example.ja: 強風のため、今日の船はすべて欠航となった。
example.en: All of today's ferries were cancelled due to strong winds.

expressions.nuance: Of wind: to rage fiercely; a written, desolate image.

example.ja: 冷たい風が吹きすさぶ中、彼は一人で待っていた。
example.en: He waited alone as the cold wind raged.

clusters.description: Snow falling and lying; expressions differ by flake size and amount, the stillness or violence of the scene, and seasonal or poetic flavor.

expressions.nuance: The first snow of the season.

example.ja: 今朝、この町に今年の初雪が降った。
example.en: This morning, the first snow of the year fell on this town.

expressions.nuance: Fine, dry, powdery snow.

example.ja: さらさらした粉雪が、街灯の光の中で舞っている。
example.en: Fine powdery snow is dancing in the light of the streetlamp.

expressions.nuance: Of snow: to fall lightly and sparsely in flurries.

example.ja: 朝から、灰色の空に雪がちらついている。
example.en: Snow has been flurrying from the grey sky since morning.

expressions.nuance: The light crunch of stepping on fresh snow.

example.ja: 誰も歩いていない新雪を、さくさく踏んで歩いた。
example.en: I crunched through the untouched fresh snow.

expressions.nuance: Thaw; snow melting as spring comes.

example.ja: 春になると、雪解けの水が川に流れ込む。
example.en: In spring, snowmelt flows into the river.

expressions.nuance: Large, heavy, soft flakes like peony petals, typical of wet, milder snow.

example.ja: 空から大きな牡丹雪がふわふわと落ちてきた。
example.en: Big fluffy snowflakes drifted down from the sky.

expressions.nuance: Snow falling silently and deeply, the world hushed.

example.ja: 静かな夜、雪がしんしんと降り積もっていく。
example.en: On the quiet night, snow falls silently and piles up.

expressions.nuance: To fall and pile up.

example.ja: 一晩で、雪が一メートル近く降り積もった。
example.en: Nearly a meter of snow piled up overnight.

expressions.nuance: A light covering of snow that makes the scenery look made-up.

example.ja: 目を覚ますと、遠くの山々がうっすら雪化粧していた。
example.en: When I woke, the distant mountains were lightly dusted with snow.

expressions.nuance: Snow that stays on the ground until spring.

example.ja: 十二月に降った雪が、そのまま根雪になった。
example.en: The snow that fell in December stayed on the ground all winter.

expressions.nuance: A whole landscape turned silver-white by snow.

example.ja: 朝起きると、外は一面の銀世界になっていた。
example.en: When I got up in the morning, outside had become a world of white.

expressions.nuance: Heavy snowfall, usually with disruption.

example.ja: 昨夜の大雪で、山の道路が通行止めになった。
example.en: Last night's heavy snow closed the mountain roads.

expressions.nuance: A snowstorm driven by strong wind.

example.ja: 吹雪がひどくて、一メートル先も見えない。
example.en: The blizzard is so bad I can't see a meter ahead.

clusters.description: Dawn through early morning; expressions differ by exact time (before dawn, daybreak, early morning), light and mood, and literary level.

expressions.nuance: Early in the morning, loosely; the everyday time word.

example.ja: 天気予報によると、朝方に少し雨が降るらしい。
example.en: According to the forecast, it may rain a little early in the morning.

expressions.nuance: The morning sun and its light.

example.ja: カーテンの隙間から、まぶしい朝日が差し込んだ。
example.en: Bright morning sun shone through the gap in the curtains.

expressions.nuance: Fresh and clear, like morning air; pleasant rather than cold.

example.ja: 窓を開けて、爽やかな朝の空気を吸い込んだ。
example.en: I opened the window and breathed in the fresh morning air.

expressions.nuance: Sleepy, half-open eyes just after waking.

example.ja: 寝ぼけ眼のまま、洗面所で歯を磨いた。
example.en: Still bleary-eyed, I brushed my teeth at the sink.

expressions.nuance: Early morning, often before people are about.

example.ja: 人のいない早朝の公園を、毎日走っている。
example.en: Every day I run in the empty park early in the morning.

expressions.nuance: Around dawn, as darkness gives way to light.

example.ja: 考え事をして、明け方までほとんど眠れなかった。
example.en: Lost in thought, I barely slept until dawn.

expressions.nuance: Daybreak, as the moment a new day starts.

example.ja: 私たちは夜明けとともに山小屋を出発した。
example.en: We left the mountain hut at daybreak.

expressions.nuance: For night to end and day to break.

example.ja: 話に夢中になっているうちに、夜が明けた。
example.en: While we were absorbed in talking, dawn broke.

expressions.nuance: Of the sky: to grow pale before sunrise.

example.ja: やがて東の空が、ぼんやりと白み始めた。
example.en: Before long, the eastern sky began to grow faintly pale.

expressions.nuance: Red morning sky at sunrise.

example.ja: 東の空が、朝焼けで赤く染まっていた。
example.en: The eastern sky was dyed red by the sunrise.

expressions.nuance: Thin morning mist hanging low over water or fields.

example.ja: 早朝の湖には、白い朝靄がかかっていた。
example.en: A white morning mist hung over the lake at dawn.

expressions.nuance: Before dawn; the formal term used in news reports.

example.ja: 火事は、今朝未明に住宅街で起きた。
example.en: The fire broke out in a residential area before dawn this morning.

expressions.nuance: Dawn; classical and poetic.

example.ja: 曙の空が、淡い紅色に色づいていく。
example.en: The dawn sky slowly takes on a pale crimson.

expressions.nuance: The first light of dawn; a rare poetic word.

example.ja: 東雲の空に、鳥たちの声が響き始めた。
example.en: Birdsong began to ring through the dawn sky.

clusters.description: Late afternoon into nightfall; expressions differ by stage (sun sinking, afterglow, twilight dark), color, and literary mood.

expressions.nuance: Of the sun: to start sinking in the afternoon; the very beginning of dusk.

example.ja: 日が傾いて、校庭の影が長く伸びてきた。
example.en: The sun sank lower and the schoolyard shadows stretched out.

expressions.nuance: The setting sun.

example.ja: 真っ赤な夕日が、ゆっくり海に沈んでいく。
example.en: A bright red sun slowly sinks into the sea.

expressions.nuance: Dusk; a neutral yet atmospheric word.

example.ja: 夕暮れの商店街を、一人でゆっくり歩いた。
example.en: I walked slowly alone through the shopping street at dusk.

expressions.nuance: Nightfall, often as the point by which something must happen.

example.ja: 山道は危ないから、日暮れ前に帰ろう。
example.en: The mountain path is dangerous, so let's go back before nightfall.

expressions.nuance: To get dark at the end of the day.

example.ja: 冬は五時にもなると、すぐに日が暮れる。
example.en: In winter it gets dark as soon as it's five o'clock.

expressions.nuance: Dim, not yet fully dark.

example.ja: 電気をつけていない部屋の中は、もう薄暗い。
example.en: Inside the room without the lights on, it's already dim.

expressions.nuance: Red sunset sky.

example.ja: 西の空が、夕焼けで真っ赤に染まった。
example.en: The western sky turned bright red in the sunset.

expressions.nuance: The deep madder red of an evening sky; more poetic than 赤.

example.ja: 雲の切れ間から、空が茜色に染まっていく。
example.en: Through the breaks in the clouds, the sky turns madder red.

expressions.nuance: The way home, evoking the end of the day.

example.ja: 遊び疲れた子どもたちが、家路を急いでいる。
example.en: Children tired from playing are hurrying home.

expressions.nuance: The gathering dark of evening.

example.ja: 迫る夕闇の中に、ぼんやりと人影が見えた。
example.en: A figure appeared faintly in the gathering dusk.

expressions.nuance: Twilight; poetic, often with a wistful mood.

example.ja: 黄昏の街に、ぽつぽつと明かりがともり始めた。
example.en: Lights began to come on one by one in the twilight town.

expressions.nuance: Of the day: to linger in dusk, slow to grow dark.

example.ja: 暮れなずむ空を、二人で黙って眺めていた。
example.en: The two of us silently watched the lingering dusk sky.

expressions.nuance: The darkness of early evening before the moon rises.

example.ja: 宵闇が、静かに小さな町を包み始めた。
example.en: Evening darkness quietly began to wrap the small town.

expressions.nuance: Dusk as the eerie hour when spirits were said to appear.

example.ja: 逢魔が時には、なぜか妙に心がざわつく。
example.en: At the eerie hour of dusk, my heart feels strangely uneasy.

clusters.description: Light and brightness; expressions differ by the kind of light (glitter, glow, glare, flicker) and its intensity.

expressions.nuance: Faint and soft, barely perceptible.

example.ja: 暗い山道の先に、ほのかな明かりが見えた。
example.en: A faint light showed at the end of the dark mountain path.

expressions.nuance: Of light: to shine in through an opening.

example.ja: 窓から、やわらかな朝の光が差し込んでいる。
example.en: Soft morning light is streaming in through the window.

expressions.nuance: To light up or illuminate.

example.ja: 古い街灯が、誰もいない夜道を照らしている。
example.en: An old streetlight illuminates the empty road at night.

expressions.nuance: Twinkling and sparkling repeatedly; a pretty, cheerful glitter.

example.ja: 日差しを受けて、湖の水面がきらきら光っている。
example.en: Catching the sunlight, the lake's surface is sparkling.

expressions.nuance: Shiny and gleaming from being clean or new, or flashing.

example.ja: 大掃除で、台所の床をぴかぴかに磨いた。
example.en: During the big cleanup, I polished the kitchen floor until it gleamed.

expressions.nuance: Sunlight filtering through leaves.

example.ja: 夏の森の中、木漏れ日を浴びながら歩いた。
example.en: I walked through the summer forest, bathed in dappled sunlight.

expressions.nuance: Of stars or distant lights: to twinkle on and off.

example.ja: 遠くの岬で、灯台の光が小さく瞬いていた。
example.en: Far off on the cape, the lighthouse light was twinkling faintly.

expressions.nuance: To glitter brilliantly; more poetic than きらきら.

example.ja: 丘の上から、きらめく街の灯を見下ろした。
example.en: From the hill I looked down on the glittering city lights.

expressions.nuance: To shine brightly; also figurative for radiance.

example.ja: 山の上では、無数の星が夜空に輝いている。
example.en: Up in the mountains, countless stars shine in the night sky.

expressions.nuance: Flickering irritatingly, or an eye-straining glare.

example.ja: 古い蛍光灯がちかちかして、目が疲れる。
example.en: The old fluorescent light flickers and tires my eyes.

expressions.nuance: Dazzlingly bright, hard to look at directly.

example.ja: 外に出ると、夏の日差しが目に眩しかった。
example.en: When I went outside, the summer sunlight dazzled my eyes.

expressions.nuance: Brilliantly dazzling; more literary than 眩しい and often admiring.

example.ja: 扉が開くと、まばゆい光に思わず目を閉じた。
example.en: When the door opened, I shut my eyes at the dazzling light.

expressions.nuance: Brightly and brilliantly lit (煌々と), often of artificial lights at night.

example.ja: 深夜になっても、店の明かりが煌々とついている。
example.en: Even late at night, the shop's lights are blazing.

expressions.nuance: Of sunshine: pouring down brilliantly and generously (燦々と).

example.ja: 南の島では、太陽が燦々と降り注いでいた。
example.en: On the southern island, the sun was pouring down brilliantly.

clusters.description: Silence and hushed places; expressions differ by whether the quiet is peaceful, deserted, tense or sudden, and by literary level.

expressions.nuance: Quietness; the plain noun for a calm, soundless atmosphere.

example.ja: 雪の降った朝の静けさが、私は好きだ。
example.en: I love the stillness of a morning after snowfall.

expressions.nuance: Whispering in hushed tones so others won't hear; about voices, not places.

example.ja: 後ろの席で、誰かがひそひそ話している。
example.en: Someone in the seats behind is whispering.

expressions.nuance: Quiet and calm in manner; used mostly of people, not places.

example.ja: 彼は物静かだが、芯の強い人だ。
example.en: He's quiet, but a person of strong character.

expressions.nuance: Hushed and deserted, as if keeping out of sight; often with a lonely feel.

example.ja: 山奥の村は、冬になるとひっそりとしている。
example.en: The village deep in the mountains grows hushed in winter.

expressions.nuance: Quiet and peaceful, used of residential areas; a positive, formal description.

example.ja: 駅から少し離れた閑静な住宅街に住んでいる。
example.en: I live in a quiet residential area a little way from the station.

expressions.nuance: Without a sound; describes how something moves or happens.

example.ja: 窓の外では、雪が音もなく降り続いている。
example.en: Outside the window, snow keeps falling without a sound.

expressions.nuance: Utterly silent, often suddenly, as everyone stops making noise.

example.ja: 先生が入ってくると、教室がしんと静まった。
example.en: When the teacher came in, the classroom went completely silent.

expressions.nuance: Deserted and quiet because few people are around; implies emptiness, not peace.

example.ja: 平日の遊園地は、驚くほど閑散としていた。
example.en: On a weekday the amusement park was surprisingly deserted.

expressions.nuance: To fall silent and lie low; also of activity or trends dying down.

example.ja: 先生に叱られて、騒いでいた生徒たちが鳴りを潜めた。
example.en: Scolded by the teacher, the noisy students fell silent.

expressions.nuance: To fall completely silent; stronger and more total than 静まる.

example.ja: 名前が呼ばれる直前、観客席が静まり返った。
example.en: Just before the name was called, the audience fell completely silent.

expressions.nuance: Hushed all at once, as when a crowd suddenly goes silent in tension or awe.

example.ja: 彼が話し始めると、会場は水を打ったように静かになった。
example.en: When he began to speak, the hall fell into a hush.

expressions.nuance: Deep, pervasive silence; a written word with a solemn feel.

example.ja: 突然の犬の鳴き声が、夜の静寂を破った。
example.en: A dog's sudden barking broke the silence of the night.

expressions.nuance: Profoundly still and hushed, as in a forest or temple grounds; literary.

example.ja: 森閑とした寺の境内に、自分の足音だけが響く。
example.en: Only my own footsteps echo in the hushed temple grounds.

clusters.description: Sounds and noises; expressions differ by source and quality of the sound (footsteps, rustling, rumbling, clamor) and by volume.

expressions.nuance: Faint and barely audible; about how weak the sound is.

example.ja: 目を閉じると、かすかに波の音が聞こえる。
example.en: When I close my eyes, I can faintly hear the waves.

expressions.nuance: An unidentified noise, often suspicious, from something moving.

example.ja: 夜中に、誰もいない台所で物音がした。
example.en: In the middle of the night there was a noise in the empty kitchen.

expressions.nuance: Dry, light rustling, as of leaves or paper.

example.ja: 風が吹くたびに、落ち葉がかさかさと鳴った。
example.en: Every time the wind blew, the fallen leaves rustled.

expressions.nuance: Light, regular tapping, as of hard heels or a knock.

example.ja: 静かな廊下から、こつこつと靴音が聞こえる。
example.en: I can hear footsteps tapping in the quiet corridor.

expressions.nuance: To resound or echo, filling a space.

example.ja: 誰もいない体育館に、ボールの音が響いた。
example.en: The sound of the ball echoed through the empty gym.

expressions.nuance: A murmuring hubbub of many voices, or rustling; restless rather than loud.

example.ja: 発表の直前、会場がざわざわし始めた。
example.en: Just before the announcement, a murmur spread through the hall.

expressions.nuance: An echo returning from mountains or valleys (こだまする).

example.ja: 山の頂上で叫ぶと、声が谷にこだました。
example.en: When I shouted from the summit, my voice echoed through the valley.

expressions.nuance: Noisy, overlapping chatter of a crowd; louder and more annoying than ざわざわ.

example.ja: 休み時間の教室は、いつもがやがやとうるさい。
example.en: The classroom at break time is always noisy with chatter.

expressions.nuance: Deep, rolling rumbling, as of distant thunder.

example.ja: 空が暗くなり、遠くで雷がごろごろ鳴り始めた。
example.en: The sky darkened and thunder began rumbling in the distance.

expressions.nuance: Noise as a nuisance, e.g. from traffic or construction; a neutral, somewhat technical word.

example.ja: 隣の工事の騒音で、昼間も眠れない。
example.en: I can't sleep even in the daytime because of the construction noise next door.

expressions.nuance: To ring out loudly and far, as a bell or alarm.

example.ja: 真夜中に突然、非常ベルが鳴り響いた。
example.en: In the middle of the night, the alarm bell suddenly rang out.

expressions.nuance: Shrill, piercing and alarming.

example.ja: けたたましいサイレンの音で、目が覚めた。
example.en: I was woken by the shrill sound of a siren.

expressions.nuance: Ear-splitting; so loud it seems to pierce the ears.

example.ja: 耳をつんざくような爆音が、あたりに響いた。
example.en: An ear-splitting blast echoed all around.

expressions.nuance: To roar or thunder with a deep, powerful sound; written.

example.ja: 夜明け前、激しい雷鳴が山々に轟いた。
example.en: Before dawn, violent thunder roared over the mountains.

clusters.description: Hot weather and heat; expressions differ by the kind of heat (humid, blazing sun, lingering) and its strength.

expressions.nuance: Pleasantly warm, like spring sunshine; always comfortable, never oppressive.

example.ja: 春の日差しで、縁側がぽかぽかと暖かい。
example.en: The veranda is pleasantly warm in the spring sunshine.

expressions.nuance: To be slightly sweaty; mild heat felt on the skin.

example.ja: 五月なのに、少し歩いただけで汗ばんだ。
example.en: Even though it was May, I got sweaty after only a short walk.

expressions.nuance: Damp and humid, with an unpleasant clammy feel; more about moisture than heat.

example.ja: 梅雨の時期は、家の中までじめじめしている。
example.en: During the rainy season, even inside the house is damp.

expressions.nuance: Muggy and sticky, hot and humid together; focuses on the heat.

example.ja: エアコンが壊れて、部屋の中がむしむしする。
example.en: The air conditioner broke and it's muggy in the room.

expressions.nuance: Hot and humid; the standard adjective for muggy weather.

example.ja: 今日は朝から風がなくて、とても蒸し暑い。
example.en: There's been no wind since morning and it's very muggy.

expressions.nuance: Hard to sleep because of the heat.

example.ja: 夜になっても気温が下がらず、寝苦しい夜だった。
example.en: The temperature didn't drop even at night; it was hard to sleep.

expressions.nuance: Lingering late-summer heat after summer should be over.

example.ja: 九月に入っても、厳しい残暑が続いている。
example.en: Even into September, the fierce late-summer heat continues.

expressions.nuance: Slow, relentless scorching of the sun on the skin.

example.ja: 日陰がなく、太陽がじりじりと肌を焼く。
example.en: There's no shade, and the sun slowly scorches my skin.

expressions.nuance: Of the sun: to beat down fiercely.

example.ja: 真夏の日差しが、容赦なく照りつける。
example.en: The midsummer sun beats down mercilessly.

expressions.nuance: Harsh, glaring brightness of a fierce sun.

example.ja: 真夏の太陽が、アスファルトをぎらぎら照らす。
example.en: The midsummer sun glares harshly on the asphalt.

expressions.nuance: To swelter; used as うだるような暑さ for exhausting heat.

example.ja: 連日、うだるような暑さが続いている。
example.en: The sweltering heat has continued day after day.

expressions.nuance: Under the blazing sun, outdoors in the heat of the day.

example.ja: 野球部は炎天下で練習を続けていた。
example.en: The baseball team kept practicing under the blazing sun.

expressions.nuance: Severe heat; a news and weather term for a heat wave.

example.ja: 今年の夏は、記録的な猛暑になった。
example.en: This summer turned out to be a record heat wave.

expressions.nuance: Scorching, burning heat; written and dramatic.

example.ja: 灼熱の砂漠を、三日かけて歩いて越えた。
example.en: We crossed the scorching desert on foot over three days.

clusters.description: Cold weather and chill; expressions differ by how bitter the cold is, whether it is felt on the skin or in the bones, and literary level.

expressions.nuance: Chilly on the skin; the mild cold of autumn mornings and evenings.

example.ja: 十月に入って、朝晩は肌寒くなってきた。
example.en: Now that it's October, mornings and evenings have become chilly.

expressions.nuance: Slightly and vaguely cold, often with a dreary feel.

example.ja: 日が差さない、薄ら寒い曇りの日だった。
example.en: It was a sunless, chilly, overcast day.

expressions.nuance: Cool to the touch, often pleasantly so.

example.ja: 夏の昼間、石の床がひんやりして気持ちいい。
example.en: On a summer afternoon, the stone floor feels nice and cool.

expressions.nuance: Of temperature: to drop sharply, especially at night or in the morning.

example.ja: 天気予報では、今夜はかなり冷え込むそうだ。
example.en: The forecast says it will get quite cold tonight.

expressions.nuance: Chilly throughout, with a bleak, empty feel.

example.ja: 暖房のない部屋は、冷え冷えとしていた。
example.en: The unheated room was cold and cheerless.

expressions.nuance: Penetrating cold that rises from the ground and chills to the core.

example.ja: 盆地にある京都の冬は、底冷えがする。
example.en: Winter in Kyoto, lying in a basin, is bitterly cold.

expressions.nuance: Of hands and feet: to go numb and stiff with cold.

example.ja: 手袋を忘れて、寒さで指がかじかんだ。
example.en: I forgot my gloves and my fingers went numb with cold.

expressions.nuance: Shivering or trembling from cold.

example.ja: バスを待つ間、寒くてぶるぶる震えていた。
example.en: While waiting for the bus, I was shivering with cold.

expressions.nuance: To be frozen stiff; the body suffering from cold.

example.ja: 凍えた手に、何度も息を吹きかけた。
example.en: I blew on my frozen hands again and again.

expressions.nuance: Biting, as if the cold were cutting one's body; usually of wind.

example.ja: 外に出ると、身を切るような風が吹いていた。
example.en: When I went out, a biting wind was blowing.

expressions.nuance: Chilling to the bone; cold felt deep inside.

example.ja: 北国の冬は、骨身に染みる寒さが続く。
example.en: Winter in the north brings bone-chilling cold.

expressions.nuance: To shake violently, from extreme cold or fear.

example.ja: 吹雪の中で、あまりの寒さに震え上がった。
example.en: In the blizzard, I shook violently from the extreme cold.

expressions.nuance: To freeze hard; a literary image of frozen ground and air.

example.ja: 凍てつく冬の夜道を、一人で歩いて帰った。
example.en: I walked home alone along the frozen winter road at night.

expressions.nuance: Severe, extreme cold; a formal written word.

example.ja: 厳寒の地で、彼らは長い冬を越した。
example.en: They got through the long winter in a land of bitter cold.

clusters.description: Busy, crowded places; expressions differ by whether the crowd feels lively and pleasant or packed and uncomfortable, and by formality.

expressions.nuance: Foot traffic; how many people pass along a street.

example.ja: この道は、夜になると人通りが少なくなる。
example.en: This street gets few passers-by at night.

expressions.nuance: The busy shopping and entertainment district of a city.

example.ja: 夜の繁華街は、ネオンの光で明るい。
example.en: The downtown entertainment district is bright with neon at night.

expressions.nuance: To bustle with people in a lively, positive way.

example.ja: 週末の商店街は、買い物客で賑わっている。
example.en: On weekends the shopping street is bustling with shoppers.

expressions.nuance: Energy and liveliness of a place or its people.

example.ja: 朝の魚市場は、いつも活気にあふれている。
example.en: The morning fish market is always full of life.

expressions.nuance: A crowd of people, usually as something to get through or avoid.

example.ja: 駅前の人混みをかき分けて、改札へ急いだ。
example.en: I pushed through the crowd in front of the station and hurried to the gate.

expressions.nuance: A crowd gathered around something to watch.

example.ja: 新しい店の前に、朝から人だかりができている。
example.en: A crowd has gathered in front of the new shop since morning.

expressions.nuance: Congestion; a formal, announcement-style word for crowding.

example.ja: 連休中は、高速道路の混雑が予想されます。
example.en: Expressway congestion is expected during the holidays.

expressions.nuance: To be packed and chaotic, people milling everywhere.

example.ja: 年末の駅は、帰省客でごった返していた。
example.en: At year's end the station was jammed with people heading home.

expressions.nuance: Packed tight like sushi in a box: uncomfortably crammed.

example.ja: 朝のバスはすし詰めで、身動きもできない。
example.en: The morning bus is packed so tight you can't move.

expressions.nuance: Pushing and shoving in a crush of people.

example.ja: 押し合いへし合いしながら、満員電車に乗り込んだ。
example.en: Pushing and shoving, we squeezed onto the packed train.

expressions.nuance: A huge success with a big turnout; always positive.

example.ja: 初日のイベントは、予想以上の大盛況だった。
example.en: The first day of the event was a bigger success than expected.

expressions.nuance: A dense mass of people, as in 黒山の人だかり.

example.ja: 事故の現場には、黒山の人だかりができていた。
example.en: A huge crowd had gathered at the scene of the accident.

expressions.reading: りっすいのよちもない
expressions.nuance: So packed there's no room to stand even an awl; a formal set phrase.

example.ja: 会場は立錐の余地もないほど、人であふれていた。
example.en: The venue was so full there was no room to stand.

clusters.description: The sea and shore; expressions differ by part of the scene (shoreline, horizon, open ocean), the sea's mood (calm or rough) and literary level.

expressions.nuance: The open water offshore, away from the beach.

example.ja: 浜辺から、沖に浮かぶ小さな船が見える。
example.en: From the beach you can see a small boat floating offshore.

expressions.nuance: The water's edge where waves wash the shore.

example.ja: 子どもたちは波打ち際で、貝殻を拾っている。
example.en: The children are picking up shells at the water's edge.

expressions.nuance: The horizon line at sea.

example.ja: オレンジ色の夕日が、水平線に沈んでいく。
example.en: The orange sun sinks below the horizon.

expressions.nuance: The salty breeze off the sea.

example.ja: 海沿いの道を、潮風に吹かれながら歩いた。
example.en: I walked along the coast road in the sea breeze.

expressions.nuance: Of waves: to roll in and break on the shore.

example.ja: 静かな浜辺に、小さな波が打ち寄せている。
example.en: Small waves are rolling in on the quiet beach.

expressions.nuance: A dead calm, with no wind and a flat sea.

example.ja: 今日の海は凪で、まるで鏡のようだ。
example.en: Today the sea is dead calm, just like a mirror.

expressions.nuance: The sound of the sea and its waves; poetic.

example.ja: 宿の窓を開けて、潮騒を聞きながら眠った。
example.en: I opened the inn's window and fell asleep to the sound of the sea.

expressions.nuance: Deep azure blue of sea or sky; written.

example.ja: 丘を越えると、紺碧の海が目の前に広がった。
example.en: Over the hill, a deep blue sea spread before us.

expressions.nuance: Whitecaps; waves breaking white in the wind.

example.ja: 風が強くなり、沖に白波が立ち始めた。
example.en: The wind picked up and whitecaps began to rise offshore.

expressions.nuance: Of the sea: to become rough and stormy.

example.ja: 台風の影響で、海が朝から荒れている。
example.en: Because of the typhoon, the sea has been rough since morning.

expressions.nuance: Rough, heavy waves; also figurative for life's hardships.

example.ja: 小さな漁船は、荒波にもまれながら進んだ。
example.en: The small fishing boat pressed on, tossed by rough waves.

expressions.nuance: A violent storm at sea that keeps boats in port.

example.ja: 大時化のため、三日間漁に出られなかった。
example.en: Because of the storm at sea, we couldn't go fishing for three days.

expressions.nuance: Of waves: to surge and churn violently; literary.

example.ja: 逆巻く波が、岩にぶつかって白く砕けた。
example.en: Surging waves crashed white against the rocks.

expressions.nuance: The vast, open ocean; grand and literary.

example.ja: 船はゆっくりと、果てしない大海原へ出ていった。
example.en: The ship slowly set out into the endless ocean.

clusters.description: How time goes by; expressions differ by speed (in a flash vs long years), emotional coloring (nostalgia, urgency) and formality.

expressions.nuance: Before one knows it; time passing unnoticed.

example.ja: 本を読んでいたら、いつの間にか外は暗くなっていた。
example.en: While I was reading, it had grown dark outside before I knew it.

expressions.nuance: In a flash; time feeling surprisingly short.

example.ja: 楽しかった夏休みは、あっという間に終わった。
example.en: The fun summer vacation was over in a flash.

expressions.nuance: Time as months and days going by, often with nostalgia.

example.ja: あの日から、ずいぶん長い月日が流れた。
example.en: A great deal of time has passed since that day.

expressions.nuance: The elapse of time; a formal, factual word.

example.ja: 事故が起きてから、ちょうど一年が経過した。
example.en: Exactly one year has passed since the accident.

expressions.nuance: A brief moment, usually of something welcome that soon ends.

example.ja: 忙しい毎日の中で、束の間の休息を楽しんだ。
example.en: In my busy days, I enjoyed a brief moment of rest.

expressions.nuance: In the blink of an eye; a little more written than あっという間.

example.ja: その噂は、瞬く間に学校中に広まった。
example.en: The rumor spread through the whole school in the blink of an eye.

expressions.nuance: Moment by moment, with a sense of urgency.

example.ja: 締め切りが、刻一刻と近づいてくる。
example.en: The deadline draws closer by the moment.

expressions.nuance: Of a clock: to tick away time; also time marching on.

example.ja: 古い柱時計が、今も静かに時を刻んでいる。
example.en: The old grandfather clock still quietly ticks away the time.

expressions.nuance: To pass by and be gone for good; used for the past.

example.ja: 過ぎ去った学生時代を、懐かしく思い出す。
example.en: I fondly remember my student days, now long gone.

expressions.nuance: Years, as a long span of time; formal and weighty.

example.ja: この橋は、十年の歳月をかけて完成した。
example.en: This bridge took ten years to complete.

expressions.nuance: To change and fade gradually with time, as seasons or feelings; literary.

example.ja: 庭の木々を見ていると、季節が移ろうのがわかる。
example.en: Watching the trees in the garden, you can see the seasons change.

expressions.nuance: The feeling that times have changed so much it seems another age.

example.ja: 子どもの頃と比べると、隔世の感がある。
example.en: Compared with my childhood, it feels like a different era.

expressions.nuance: Days of old; used as 昔日の面影 for what has been lost.

example.ja: 開発が進んだこの町に、昔日の面影はない。
example.en: In this redeveloped town, no trace of the old days remains.

expressions.nuance: Proverb: time flies like an arrow.

example.ja: 光陰矢の如しで、もう卒業して十年になる。
example.en: Time flies; it's already been ten years since I graduated.
